title: Addressing an Audience with Formal Courtesy

sections.content:
You know *tú*, *usted* and *don* and *doña* for one-to-one address from B2 Unit 34, and plural *ustedes* from A1 Unit 8. When speaking from a podium to a live audience in Latin American Spanish, the standard form is plural *ustedes* across every register — from a university seminar to a formal auditorium.

Maintaining courtesy on stage depends on two habits. First, open with a formal vocative followed by a comma (*estimados asistentes*, *distinguido público*, *señoras y señores*). Second, keep *ustedes* agreement completely consistent across verbs, imperatives (*permítanme señalar*, *consideren por un momento*), object pronouns (*les agradezco*, *los invito*) and possessives (*su atención*, *sus preguntas*).

A common slip in long speeches is drifting mid-sentence from *ustedes* to singular *tú* (*piensen en tu futuro*) or mixing singular and plural imperatives.

sections.title: Formal audience address (*ustedes*)
rows: *Permítanme empezar con una pregunta.* / *Consideren este ejemplo.*
*Les pido que compartan sus inquietudes.* (not *te pido* / *tus*)
*Quisiera invitarlos a reflexionar…* / *Les ruego que escuchen…*

items.spanish: Estimados asistentes, les agradezco de antemano su presencia en este auditorio.
items.english: Esteemed attendees, I thank you in advance for your presence in this auditorium.

items.spanish: Distinguido público, permítanme subir al estrado con una sola pregunta.
items.english: Distinguished audience, allow me to step up to the podium with a single question.

items.spanish: Les pido que escuchen con mente atenta y compartan sus observaciones al final.
items.english: I ask you to listen with an attentive mind and share your observations at the end.

items.spanish: Un orador cortés mantiene siempre el mismo trato hacia quienes lo escuchan.
items.english: A courteous speaker always keeps the same form of address towards those listening.

sections.content: Always check that every verb, clitic (*les/los*) and possessive (*su/sus*) stays in *ustedes*: never mix *ustedes* with *tú* (*les pido que revises tus notas* is an abrupt register break). In formal openings, place a comma after the vocative (*Estimados asistentes,*).
